Explain how a VPN works in simple words
8:10 AM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, so nobody in between can see what you send.

Without one, your traffic goes through your internet provider or the café Wi-Fi, and they can see which sites you visit. With one, your data is locked (encrypted) and sent to the VPN company's computer first. That computer then talks to the website for you.

Two things follow from this:

Websites see the VPN's location, not yours.
Your internet provider sees only scrambled data going to the VPN, not what is inside it.

It does not make you invisible. The VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust.
